hints: Notice the atom collides normally and rebounds along its original path, so motion stays on one line but direction reverses.
Recall momentum $p = mv$ is a vector, so assign opposite signs to motion toward the wall and motion away from the wall.
Form the change as $\Delta p = p_{final} - p_{initial}$ with those opposite signs and find its magnitude.
walkthrough: Take the direction toward the wall as positive. The initial momentum arriving with speed $v$ is $p_{initial} = +mv$.
The collision is perfectly elastic with a fixed wall, so no kinetic energy is lost and the atom rebounds with the same speed $v$ along the same line but in the opposite direction.
Therefore the final momentum is $p_{final} = -mv$ because velocity has reversed sign.
Change in momentum is final minus initial: $\Delta p = p_{final} - p_{initial} = -mv - (+mv) = -2mv$.
The magnitude of the change is $2mv$, which ignores the negative sign that only shows direction. This is option D.

options.A: Speed is unchanged but velocity reverses, so vector momentum cannot be unchanged.
options.B: Halving $mv$ has no physical basis here since the atom reverses the full $mv$ to $-mv$.
options.C: This is the magnitude of the initial or final momentum alone, not the vector difference between them.
options.D: Reversal from $+mv$ to $-mv$ gives a magnitude change of $2mv$.
